arguments: Operation handle is written before allocation success, potentially exposing stale or client-chosen handles on setup failure
message.text: Operation handle is written before allocation success, potentially exposing stale or client-chosen handles on setup failure

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: The finding is valid because the hash setup path writes iov->op_handle into out_vec[0] before allocation succeeds and returns allocation errors without clearing that output. Evidence: secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:140-148 performs the pre-allocation write and allocation call, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:169-182 returns non-success status without clearing out_vec[0], and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:89-92 shows allocation can fail immediately when the prewritten handle is nonzero. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Only write the newly allocated handle to out_vec[0] after tfm_crypto_operation_alloc returns success, or clear out_vec[0] / set out_vec[0].len to 0 on allocation failure. Ensure allocation APIs do not rely on pre-populated untrusted handle values unless explicitly intended and validated.
properties.reasoning: In the hash setup path, the response handle is initialized from the caller-supplied iov->op_handle before tfm_crypto_operation_alloc succeeds. If allocation later fails, this function returns the error without clearing out_vec[0]. The comments later in the file show that out_vec[0] is reflected back to the client for some operations, so a failure path may return a handle value that was not successfully allocated by this call. Depending on how clients or handle management treat this value, this could create stale-handle confusion across the secure/non-secure boundary. The exact impact depends on tfm_crypto_operation_alloc and the caller contract, which are not present in this file.
